Winter cash assistance
PLAN

550,000 people

Period
Winter 2024-2025; September 2024 plan

UNHCR: Ukraine Winter Response Plan 2024-2025, updated September 2024

Where to find it
PDF p. 1, cash support

UNHCR REPORTED

258,345 people

Period
September 2024-March 2025 summary; April cash narrative specifies October-March

UNHCR: UNHCR Ukraine Winter Response 2024-2025: Post Distribution Monitoring Key Findings (July 2025)

Where to find it
PDF p. 1, Cash Assistance row and footnotes

Assessment
46.97% of original people target

The plan also gives 263,000 households. That is a different unit, not the denominator used here. Figures are UNHCR self-reports and remain subject to verification.

Follow-up
Kharkiv reported a regional resource ceiling and bank-detail checks; the Ministry separately reported technical payment failures. A later appeal judgment upheld a finding that Snovsk list/control failures deprived at least 90 residents of the opportunity for aid. FCDO recommends earlier UNHCR winter funding. These are specific constraints with different scopes. No obtained record apportions the national 291,655-person gap, and residents or households cannot replace people in that calculation.

Sources: Why fewer than half of Kharkiv winter-cash applicants received UAH 21,000 · Households in frontline regions to receive additional funds for heating season · Snovsk winter-aid list failures: appeal judgment in case 620/6119/25 · Snovsk announces UNHCR solid-fuel assistance registration · HARP annual review, S40017629, dated 16 November 2025

Calculation
258,345 / 550,000 × 100 = 46.97%; difference: 291,655 people.

Period

UNHCR: Ukraine Winter Response Plan 2024-2025, updated September 2024

Where to find it
PDF p. 1, alternative energy

UNHCR REPORTED

186 generators

Period
Winter period; July 2025 report, box gives no separate cutoff

UNHCR: UNHCR Ukraine Winter Response 2024-2025: Post Distribution Monitoring Key Findings (July 2025)

Where to find it
PDF p. 4, Alternative Energy Support box

Assessment
44.29% of original generator target

April reports 110; July reports 186 during the winter period. The reports do not provide a reconciled delivery chronology or comparable generator cutoffs.

Follow-up
Correction: the April footnote dates people reached to 31 March, not generator units. A signed agreement effective 28 January lists one generator, but does not identify its membership in either national count or establish its physical delivery date. The 76-unit difference still cannot be assigned to later deliveries, wider coverage or revised records. Neither total is labelled final here.

Sources: UNHCR Ukraine Delivery Updates - 14 April 2025 · UNHCR Ukraine Winter Response 2024-2025: Post Distribution Monitoring Key Findings (July 2025) · Signed UNHCR generator ownership-transfer agreement KYIV_GEN_18_2025

Calculation
186 / 420 × 100 = 44.29%; difference: 234 generators.

claim_23:
REPORT
SUPPORTED BY CITED SOURCE
On 5 November 2025, an appeal court upheld a finding that failures in compiling beneficiary lists, checking addresses/duplicates and notifying excluded applicants in Snovsk deprived at least 90 residents of the opportunity to receive UAH 21,000 in winter solid-fuel assistance. A contemporaneous council notice identifies the programme as UNHCR-backed.

Limits
This is a local administrative judgment about a disciplinary measure. It concerns residents and lost opportunity, not 90 households, a criminal conviction or a verified payment ledger. The appeal was dismissed; no later cassation was located, which does not prove none exists. The record does not show how these residents map to UNHCR’s national reported reach or quantify any part of the 291,655-person target gap.

Where to find it
Appeal judgment, findings on December lists, concluding 90-resident reasoning and operative outcome; council registration notice dated 16 December 2024, opening programme paragraph and no-guarantee warning.

Supporting and conflicting sources
Each link applies to the wording of this claim.
